title: MODALES EN PASADO
subtitle: Past modals · crítica, arrepentimiento y especulación

map.center: Modal + have + participio mira al pasado para criticar, lamentar o especular sobre lo que pasó… o no pasó.

nodes.title: Crítica y arrepentimiento
items: should / ought to have + participio = debería haber…
You should have told me. (No lo hiciste.)
I shouldn't have shouted. (Lo hice.)

nodes.title: ¿Hacía falta?
rows: = lo hice, pero no hacía falta

nodes.title: Posibilidad perdida
items: could have + participio = podría haber…, pero no
We could have won. (Pudimos ganar.)
Reproche: You could have called!

nodes.title: Especulación
items: might / may / could have = quizá…, puede que…
She may have missed the train.
Queja: You might have warned me!

nodes.title: Would have
items: Lo que habría pasado (condición implícita)
I would have helped, but nobody asked.
Deseo frustrado: I'd have liked to go.

nodes.title: Consejo rápido
items: Siempre have: nunca should of ni should had
Continua: should have been + -ing
Pasiva: should have been + participio

error.title: Error común
bad: You must have told me! (= deberías)

mini.es: Completa con un modal en pasado.

items.q: You ____ (tell) me! I'd have helped.
I ____ (buy) milk: we had plenty.
We ____ (win), but we didn't.
She ____ (miss) the bus. I'm not sure.
I ____ (like) to come, but I was ill.

explain.es: Los modales en pasado se forman siempre igual: modal + have + participio. Sirven para mirar atrás y opinar sobre lo ocurrido: criticar o lamentar (should have), señalar que algo no hacía falta (needn't have), hablar de oportunidades perdidas (could have), especular (might / may have) o imaginar lo que habría pasado (would have). Casi todos se refieren a algo que, en realidad, no ocurrió. Es una estructura clave en C1, tanto en conversación (reproches, disculpas) como en textos formales (informes, análisis de errores).
explain.en: Past modals always follow the pattern modal + have + past participle. We use them to look back and comment: criticism, regret, unnecessary actions, missed opportunities, speculation and hypothetical results.
formula: should / ought to / needn't / could / might / may / would + *have done*

explain.title: 1 · Should have / ought to have
explain.es: should have + participio (debería haber…) indica que algo era lo correcto pero no se hizo: sirve para criticar a otros o lamentarnos. En negativa, shouldn't have indica que algo se hizo y estuvo mal. ought to have significa lo mismo, con un matiz algo más formal o moral; su negativa, oughtn't to have, es poco frecuente. La expresión I should have known equivale a tendría que habérmelo imaginado.
explain.en: should have + participle: the right thing didn't happen (criticism or regret). shouldn't have: it happened and it was a mistake. ought to have is similar, slightly more formal.

examples.en: You should have told me you were coming — I'd have made dinner.
examples.es: Deberías haberme dicho que venías: habría hecho la cena.

examples.en: I shouldn't have sent that email in the heat of the moment.
examples.es: No debería haber enviado ese correo en caliente.

examples.en: The government ought to have consulted the unions before the reform.
examples.es: El Gobierno debería haber consultado a los sindicatos antes de la reforma.

examples.en: I should have known he wouldn't turn up.
examples.es: Tendría que habérmelo imaginado: no iba a aparecer.

explain.title: 2 · Needn't have / didn't need to
explain.es: Esta es la gran sutileza del tema. needn't have + participio = lo hice, pero no hacía falta (esfuerzo inútil). didn't need to + infinitivo = no era necesario; normalmente significa que no lo hice, aunque el contexto puede indicar lo contrario (I didn't need to wait, but I did). didn't have to funciona igual que didn't need to. needn't have es más británico y algo más formal.
explain.en: needn't have done: it was done, but it was unnecessary. didn't need to do: it wasn't necessary (and usually wasn't done).
formula: *didn't need to* + infinitivo → no hacía falta

examples.en: You needn't have brought a present — but thank you!
examples.es: No tenías que haber traído nada… ¡pero gracias!

examples.en: I needn't have revised so much: the exam was a piece of cake.
examples.es: No hacía falta que estudiara tanto: el examen estaba chupado.

examples.en: We didn't need to book a table, so we just turned up.
examples.es: No hacía falta reservar mesa, así que nos presentamos sin más.

explain.title: NEEDN'T HAVE o DIDN'T NEED TO
explain.title_en: needn't have vs didn't need to
explain.es: Pregúntate: ¿se hizo la acción? Si se hizo y fue inútil → needn't have. Si no se hizo porque no hacía falta → didn't need to.
explain.en: Ask yourself: was the action actually done?

cols.head: ✅ Lo hice (en vano)
items: I needn't have taken a taxi: the hotel was round the corner.
Cogí un taxi, pero no hacía falta.
She needn't have worried. (Se preocupó en vano.)

cols.head: 🚫 No lo hice
items: I didn't need to take a taxi: Ana gave me a lift.
No cogí taxi: no hacía falta.
We didn't have to queue. (No hicimos cola.)

explain.title: 3 · Could have
explain.es: could have + participio (podría haber…, pude haber…) habla de algo que era posible pero no ocurrió: oportunidades perdidas, peligros evitados o capacidades no aprovechadas. Con tono de queja es un reproche: You could have warned me! (¡podrías haberme avisado!). couldn't have + comparativo es enfático: I couldn't have been happier (no podría haber estado más feliz). Y couldn't have también expresa que algo era imposible: I couldn't have done it without you.
explain.en: could have + participle: possible, but it didn't happen; with a complaining tone it is a reproach. couldn't have + comparative is emphatic; couldn't have can also mean 'impossible'.

examples.en: That was reckless — you could have been killed!
examples.es: Eso fue una imprudencia: ¡te podrías haber matado!

examples.en: She could have studied medicine, but she chose fine art.
examples.es: Podría haber estudiado Medicina, pero eligió Bellas Artes.

examples.en: You could have let me know you'd be late!
examples.es: ¡Podrías haberme avisado de que llegarías tarde!
El lanzamiento no podría haber salido mejor.

explain.title: 4 · Might / may / could have
explain.es: Para especular sobre el pasado (quizá…, puede que…) usamos might have, may have o could have + participio. may have suena algo más formal. En negativa hay diferencia: might not / may not have = puede que no, pero couldn't have = es imposible que. Además, might have (no may) sirve para un reproche irritado: You might have told me! (Las deducciones seguras con must have / can't have se trabajan en B2.)
explain.en: might / may / could have: speculation about the past. might not have = perhaps not; couldn't have = impossible. might have can also express irritation.
formula: Sujeto + *might not / may not have* + participio

examples.en: He might have missed the train — that would explain why he isn't here.
examples.es: Puede que haya perdido el tren: eso explicaría por qué no está aquí.

examples.en: The files may have been deleted by mistake.
examples.es: Puede que los archivos se borraran por error.

examples.en: She might not have received the invitation.
examples.es: Puede que no recibiera la invitación.

examples.en: You might have warned me the boss was in a foul mood!
examples.es: ¡Ya podrías haberme avisado de que el jefe estaba de un humor de perros!

explain.title: 5 · Would have
explain.es: would have + participio (habría…) describe lo que habría pasado o habríamos hecho en otras circunstancias. Muchas veces la condición está implícita (but…, otherwise, in your position), sin if. Con verbos de deseo expresa un deseo frustrado: I would have liked to + infinitivo (me habría gustado). wouldn't have + participio expresa rechazo: I wouldn't have missed it for the world. (El third conditional completo se estudia en B2.)
explain.en: would have + participle: what would have happened in different circumstances, often with an implicit condition. I would have liked to… expresses an unfulfilled wish.

examples.en: I would have helped you, but you didn't ask.
examples.es: Te habría ayudado, pero no me lo pediste.

examples.en: In your position, I wouldn't have accepted the offer.
examples.es: En tu lugar, yo no habría aceptado la oferta.

examples.en: I'd have liked to stay longer, but I had a flight to catch.
examples.es: Me habría gustado quedarme más, pero tenía que coger un vuelo.

examples.en: Luckily the alarm went off; otherwise we would have lost everything.
examples.es: Por suerte saltó la alarma; si no, lo habríamos perdido todo.

items.es: ¿Algo era lo correcto y no se hizo (o se hizo mal)? → should(n't) / ought to have.
items.en: The right thing didn't happen → should / ought to have.

items.es: ¿Algo innecesario? Si se hizo → needn't have + participio. Si no se hizo → didn't need to + infinitivo.
items.en: Unnecessary: done → needn't have; not done → didn't need to.

items.es: ¿Una oportunidad o un peligro que no se materializó? → could have.
items.en: Missed chance or danger → could have.

items.es: ¿No sabes lo que pasó y especulas? → might / may / could have.
items.en: Speculation → might / may / could have.

items.es: ¿Qué habría pasado en otras circunstancias? → would have.
items.en: Hypothetical result → would have.

items.es: Construye: modal + have + participio (o have been + -ing / have been + participio).
items.en: Build: modal + have + participle (or have been + -ing / participle).

explain.title: Resumen: ¿qué modal uso?
head: Modal + have + participio
Significado
Función
¿Ocurrió?
Ejemplo
explain.note: Clave: casi todos los modales en pasado hablan de lo que NO ocurrió. Excepciones: shouldn't have y needn't have (sí ocurrió) y la especulación (no lo sabemos).
explain.note_en: Most past modals refer to things that did NOT happen — except shouldn't have and needn't have (it did happen) and speculation (we don't know).

explain.title: COULD HAVE o WAS ABLE TO
explain.title_en: could have vs was able to
explain.es: En afirmativa, could have done = podía, pero no lo hice. Para decir que sí lo conseguí en una ocasión concreta, usamos was able to / managed to (no could).
explain.en: could have done = possible, but not done. was able to / managed to = actually done on a specific occasion.

cols.head: 🚪 could have · no lo hice
items: We could have reached the summit, but the weather turned.
Podríamos haber hecho cumbre, pero cambió el tiempo.

cols.head: 🏔️ was able to · lo logré
items: We were able to reach the summit before the storm.
Conseguimos hacer cumbre antes de la tormenta.

explain.title: Formas: simple, continua y pasiva
head: Forma
Estructura

explain.note: Ojo: should've suena /ˈʃʊdəv/ y por eso hasta muchos nativos escriben should of. ¡Es un error! Siempre have.
explain.note_en: should've sounds like 'should of' — but it is always have.

items.en: You shouldn't have!
items.es: ¡No tenías por qué! (al recibir un regalo)

items.en: I should have known.
items.es: Tendría que habérmelo imaginado.

items.en: It could have been worse.
items.es: Podría haber sido peor.

items.en: I could have kicked myself.
items.es: Me habría dado de bofetadas.

items.en: You needn't have bothered.
items.es: No hacía falta que te molestaras.

items.en: You might have said!
items.es: ¡Ya podías haberlo dicho!

items.en: I wouldn't have missed it for the world.
items.es: No me lo habría perdido por nada del mundo.

items.en: Who would have thought it?
items.es: ¿Quién lo habría dicho?

items.en: The project should have been completed by March.
items.es: El proyecto debería haberse terminado para marzo.

items.en: You shouldn't have been texting while driving.
items.es: No deberías haber estado escribiendo mensajes mientras conducías.

items.en: We needn't have hurried; the meeting started late.
items.es: No hacía falta que nos diéramos prisa: la reunión empezó tarde.

items.en: Luckily, I didn't need to show my passport.
items.es: Por suerte, no tuve que enseñar el pasaporte.

items.en: The accident could have been avoided.
items.es: El accidente se podría haber evitado.

items.en: They may have misunderstood the instructions.
items.es: Puede que hayan entendido mal las instrucciones.

items.en: I would have called, but my battery was dead.
items.es: Te habría llamado, pero me quedé sin batería.

items.en: She ought to have declared the conflict of interest.
items.es: Debería haber declarado el conflicto de intereses.

items.en: He might have been joking — it was hard to tell.
items.es: Puede que estuviera de broma; era difícil saberlo.

items.en: Should I have mentioned the deadline earlier?
items.es: ¿Debería haber mencionado antes la fecha límite?

items.en: With more funding, the study could have reached different conclusions.
items.es: Con más financiación, el estudio podría haber llegado a otras conclusiones.

items.en: Nobody would have guessed she was nervous.
items.es: Nadie habría adivinado que estaba nerviosa.

items.bad: You must have told me! <small>(= deberías)</small>
items.why: Crítica = should have. Must have = deducción (seguro que).
items.why_en: Criticism → should have, not must have.

items.why: Modal + have + participio: ¡no te comas el have!
Tras un modal va have (infinitivo), nunca had.
items.why_en: After a modal: have, never had.

items.why: Should've suena «should of», pero se escribe have.
items.why_en: It sounds like 'of', but it's have.

items.bad: I didn't need to buy bread, so I wasted my money.
items.good: I needn't have bought bread, so I wasted my money.
items.why: Lo compraste y fue inútil → needn't have.

items.bad: We could reach the summit after nine hours.
items.good: We were able to reach the summit after nine hours.
items.why: Logro concreto en el pasado → was able to / managed to.

items.bad: He mightn't have stolen it: he was abroad. <small>(= imposible)</small>
items.good: He couldn't have stolen it: he was abroad.
items.why: Imposible → couldn't have. Might not = quizá no.

lines.en: Well, that could have gone better.
lines.es: Bueno, eso podría haber salido mejor.

lines.en: I know. I should have checked the figures beforehand. The client spotted the error straight away.
lines.es: Lo sé. Debería haber comprobado las cifras antes. El cliente vio el error enseguida.

lines.en: You might have told me you hadn't had time — I'd have done it myself.
lines.es: Ya podrías haberme dicho que no habías tenido tiempo: lo habría hecho yo.

lines.en: You're right. And I needn't have printed forty copies of the report; they only wanted the summary.
lines.es: Tienes razón. Y no hacía falta que imprimiera cuarenta copias del informe: solo querían el resumen.

lines.en: Never mind. At least we didn't need to present the budget today.
lines.es: No pasa nada. Al menos hoy no hacía falta presentar el presupuesto.

lines.en: Do you think they may have lost interest?
lines.es: ¿Crees que puede que hayan perdido el interés?

lines.en: They might have, but they asked for a follow-up call, so I doubt it.
lines.es: Puede ser, pero pidieron una llamada de seguimiento, así que lo dudo.

lines.en: Then it could have been worse. Lesson learnt!
lines.es: Entonces podría haber sido peor. ¡Lección aprendida!

explain.title: Truco del «deber»
explain.es: Cuidado con el calco: deberías haber (consejo tardío, crítica) → should have. Debe de haber / seguro que (deducción) → must have. Si en español dices «podrías haber…» con tono de queja → could have o might have. Y en el habla rápida oirás should've, could've, would've /ˈʃʊdəv, ˈkʊdəv, ˈwʊdəv/: ¡pero se escriben con have!
explain.en: deberías haber → should have; debe de haber → must have; podrías haber (complaint) → could / might have.

exercises.title: Elige el modal
exercises.es: Rodea la opción correcta. Piensa: ¿pasó o no pasó?
exercises.en: Circle the correct option. Did it happen or not?

items.q: I'm exhausted. I [shouldn't have|couldn't have] stayed up so late.
You [needn't have|didn't need to] bought so much food — only four people came.
The tickets were free, so we [needn't have|didn't need to] pay.
That was dangerous! You [could have|should have] fallen!

You [ought|ought to] have consulted a lawyer.
The match [couldn't have|wouldn't have] been more exciting.

items.q: “I needn't have bought a ticket.” → I bought a ticket.
items.why: Needn't have = lo hice, pero no hacía falta.

items.q: “I didn't need to buy a ticket.” → I definitely bought a ticket.
items.why: Normalmente significa que no lo compró.

items.q: “You should have phoned.” → You phoned.
“She shouldn't have resigned.” → She resigned.
items.why: Shouldn't have = lo hizo y fue un error.

items.q: “They could have won.” → They won.
items.why: Could have = posible, pero no ocurrió.

items.q: “He may have left.” → The speaker knows he has left.
“I'd have liked to see the exhibition.” → I saw the exhibition.
“The launch couldn't have gone better.” → The launch went extremely well.

exercises.en: Read the opinion column. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
exercises.text_title: Opinion: a disaster that should never have happened
text: Last November's floods in the valley were not simply bad luck. Engineers had been warning the council for years that the river defences were inadequate, and the authorities ought to have acted on those warnings long before the storm arrived.

The council insists it could not have foreseen such extreme rainfall. That may be true, but a basic maintenance programme would have reduced the damage considerably. Several residents told this newspaper that the drains had not been cleared for months; some of the flooding might have been avoided altogether.

To its credit, the council did evacuate the care home in time — although, as it turned out, the residents needn't have been moved: the water never reached the building. Meanwhile, many families in the lower streets didn't need to be told to leave: they had seen the water rising and had already gone. What the council should have done is listen. Next time, it might not be so lucky.

items.q: The council had been warned about the river defences.
The writer believes the floods were just bad luck.
items.why: “The floods were not simply bad luck.”

items.q: According to the writer, what ought the authorities to have done?
items.a: They ought to have acted on the engineers' warnings before the storm arrived.

items.q: What would have reduced the damage considerably?
The care home residents were moved unnecessarily.
items.why: They needn't have been moved: the water never reached the building.

items.q: Why didn't the families in the lower streets need to be told to leave?
items.a: Because they had seen the water rising and had already gone.

items.q: Find a sentence that speculates about the past.
items.a: “Some of the flooding might have been avoided altogether.”

items.q: What does the writer think the council should have done?
items.a: It should have listened (to the warnings).

exercises.title: Traduce al inglés
exercises.es: Traduce. Piensa: ¿crítica, necesidad, posibilidad perdida, especulación o resultado hipotético?

items.q: Deberías habérmelo dicho antes.
a: You should have told me before.
You should have told me earlier.

items.q: No hacía falta que trajeras nada, pero gracias.
items.a: You needn't have brought anything, but thank you.

items.q: Puede que hayan perdido el vuelo.
a: They may have missed the flight.
They might have missed the flight.

items.q: ¡Podrías haberme avisado!
No debería haber dicho eso en la reunión.
items.a: I shouldn't have said that in the meeting.

items.q: Me habría gustado conocer a tus padres.
items.a: I would have liked to meet your parents.

items.q: El accidente se podría haber evitado.
items.a: The accident could have been avoided.

items.q: No tuvimos que esperar: la consulta estaba vacía.
a: We didn't need to wait: the surgery was empty.
We didn't have to wait: the surgery was empty.

items.q: El Gobierno debería haber actuado antes.
a: The government should have acted earlier.
The government ought to have acted sooner.

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Escribe sobre tu experiencia con modales en pasado.
exercises.en: Write about your own experience using past modals.

items.q: Escribe dos cosas de las que te arrepientes. (should have / shouldn't have)
items.a: Ej.: I should have studied abroad when I had the chance. I shouldn't have sold my old guitar.

items.q: Cuenta algo que hiciste y que no hacía falta. (needn't have)
items.a: Ej.: I needn't have printed my boarding pass: the airline accepted the one on my phone.

items.q: Un amigo no se presentó a una cena. Especula con tres explicaciones. (might / may / could have)
items.a: Ej.: He might have got lost. He may have forgotten. His train could have been cancelled.

items.q: Escribe un reproche educado a un compañero que no te avisó de un cambio. (could have / might have)
items.a: Ej.: You could have let me know the meeting had been moved — I'd have prepared the slides.

checklist.es: Critico y lamento con should have / ought to have.
checklist.en: I can criticise and express regret with should have / ought to have.

checklist.es: Distingo needn't have done (lo hice) de didn't need to do (no lo hice).
checklist.en: I can distinguish needn't have done and didn't need to do.

checklist.es: Uso could have para oportunidades perdidas y reproches.
checklist.en: I can use could have for missed chances and reproaches.

checklist.es: Especulo con might / may / could have y sé que couldn't have = imposible.
checklist.en: I can speculate with might / may / could have.

checklist.es: Expreso lo que habría pasado con would have y I'd have liked to.
checklist.en: I can say what would have happened.

checklist.es: Manejo la forma continua y la pasiva: should have been + -ing / participio.
checklist.en: I can use continuous and passive past modals.

checklist.es: Nunca escribo <s>should of</s>, <s>should had</s> ni <s>must have</s> para criticar.
checklist.en: I never write should of, should had or must have for criticism.
